mode_b_lead_finding: The release's own guidance paragraph contains the offset the market ignored: net capex guidance was LOWERED to 8.5-10.0% of revenue from 9.0-10.5%, explicitly because of 'the growing contribution from less capital-intensive product and service revenue.' At the $317M revenue midpoint that is ~$1.6M of capex saved against ~$1.0M of EBITDA given up -- the guidance revision is FREE-CASH-FLOW ACCRETIVE. EBITDA is the wrong metric for this mix shift. That is the honest bull point and it is real. It is NOT, however, enough to make the name a buy, because the second Mode-B finding overwhelms it: the FY26 guide is now arithmetically back-half loaded to a degree H1 gives no evidence for, and a dated regulatory documentation change on the largest revenue code lands inside the guided period unmentioned.

the_arithmetic_that_explains_minus_16.required_quarterly_ebitda_h2: avg $19.0M vs Q2-26's $13.7M = +38.6%; the all-time record quarter is Q4-25 at $18.2M, so the guide needs TWO quarters averaging ABOVE the record
the_arithmetic_that_explains_minus_16.eight_quarter_read: revenue +34.7% (58.0 -> 78.1) while adjusted EBITDA dollars went 13.95 -> 13.72, i.e. -1.6%. Two years of revenue growth have produced zero EBITDA dollars. Q2-26 is the second consecutive sequential decline off the Q4-25 peak.
the_arithmetic_that_explains_minus_16.bear_bridge: apply 2025's actual +104bp seasonal H1->H2 step to the 18.26% H1-26 base -> H2 margin 19.3% -> H2 EBITDA $31.6M -> FY26 $59.6M, which is 6.9% BELOW the low end of the guide. Even a generous +200bp step lands at $61.2M, still below the low end.
the_arithmetic_that_explains_minus_16.verdict: the -15.9% is NOT an overreaction to a $1M trim. It is the market marking the probability that the unchanged back half is unreachable. Our p(FY26 EBITDA lands inside the $64-68M guide) = 0.30-0.35.

bear_case_properly_built.a_mix_shift_as_a_trend: MODELED and BOUNDED, not a cliff. Solving segment gross margins off the mix shift gives rental+service ~59.3% GM vs equipment/supply sales ~52.8% (on a CASH basis, adding back equipment depreciation, the gap widens to roughly 72.8% vs 52.8%). Running PAP/resupply at +40%/+35%/+30%/+25% and rentals at +6%: blended cash gross margin erodes only ~80bp/yr (67.6% FY26 -> 65.3% FY29). With ~300bp/yr of SG&A leverage, blended adjusted-EBITDA margin SETTLES at 20-22% and EBITDA dollars still compound ~18%/yr (FY26 $63M -> FY29 $105M). WITHOUT SG&A leverage (SG&A grows with revenue) it settles at 18-19% and EBITDA compounds ~14%/yr. Either way mix alone does not break the business -- the swing factor is SG&A, not mix. This materially deflates the headline bear.
bear_case_properly_built.b_medicare_and_the_reimbursement_pipelin: THE REAL KILL CHANNEL, and it is neither the one the seed named nor the one the company discusses. Competitive bidding is REFUTED (next round is RID-only; VMD furnishes none of those categories; NIV/PAP/oxygen were all pulled from Round 2021 pre-implementation). Rates are BENIGN (+2.0% CY2026 DMEPOS update). What IS live: (1) CMS-6109-N published 2026-07-30 adds E0466 and E0467 to the Required Face-to-Face Encounter and Written Order Prior to Delivery List effective 2026-10-28, citing ventilators as a top-20 CERT improper-payment DMEPOS category; (2) a Qlarant UPIC extrapolated $5.9M overpayment finding on Sleep Management's E0466 monthly rentals, reduced to $2.2M, LOST at the ALJ in June 2026. Together these are one coherent mechanism: CMS is tightening documentation and integrity enforcement on exactly VMD's largest code, and VMD has already lost once. Magnitude sizing: F2F/WOPD is a condition of payment at SETUP. Historical analogues (2013-14 home-health F2F) produced 5-15% setup slowdowns and denial spikes for 2-4 quarters until referral-source workflows adapted. Applied here: Medicare vent setups are ~16% of revenue; a 10% setup slowdown for 2-3 quarters is ~1.6% of revenue at peak plus incremental documentation SG&A -- on top of an SG&A line already growing 5pp faster than revenue. Q4-26 sees only ~2 months of exposure; H1-27 is the full-exposure window. LATENCY WARNING: the Q3-26 print (~2026-11-03) lands BEFORE any material F2F/WOPD exposure, so the first true read on this channel is the Q4-26 print in ~March 2027.
bear_case_properly_built.c_ahco_supplier_price_shock: UNVERIFIABLE and bounded at <=4% of EBITDA. Could not source the $30M claim; AHCO's own -25.7% is explained by a sales miss, goodwill charge and slashed guide. VMD's Q2 cash-COGS move is fully accounted for by mix with no residual, so nothing is transmitting yet. For rental devices the cost is capitalized, so any shock hits capex over ~5 years rather than EBITDA. Do not size on this.
bear_case_properly_built.d_payer_audits_recoupments: LIVE and ADVERSE, see the Qlarant finding. The dollars ($2.2M, already paid, sitting in Prepaid) are immaterial. The MECHANISM is not: an extrapolated UPIC determination on vent medical-necessity documentation, upheld by an ALJ, is an invitation to further audits, prepayment review, and a permanently higher documentation cost per patient. Note the timing correlation (not causation): the ALJ loss was June 2026, inside the quarter in which SG&A jumped 28.9%.

honesty_alpha_finding: The catch is not a bad number -- every number reconciles to audited XBRL. The catch is takeaway-vs-data divergence by OMISSION, at the exact moment the omitted risk acquired a date. The CEO's marketed takeaway is 'multiple growth engines... confident in Viemed's ability to deliver consistent and increasingly predictable growth.' Against the company's own file on the same day: (1) 63% of the revenue growth came from resupply, not the ventilator pillar the release leads with; (2) 'record census' conceals nine months of flat-to-declining census (Jun-25 12,149 -> Mar-26 12,090, derivable purely from the company's own two disclosed growth rates); (3) an adverse ALJ ruling on extrapolated Medicare overpayments for the largest revenue code, first disclosed in the 10-Q that evening and absent from the release; (4) a CMS rule published four days earlier imposing new condition-of-payment documentation on that same code effective 2026-10-28, mentioned nowhere, while Item 1A asserts 'no material changes in our risk factors.' Each item is individually defensible; the pattern is a polished story diverging from its own data on the one axis that matters. Under the honesty-alpha doctrine that argues against paying up on the dip -- this is a name to buy lower, not a name to buy because it fell.

edge_explainer: Expected value +13.8% against a 35% branch that loses ~21%. Fair-risk with a thin edge overlay, not a fat pitch. The decisive asymmetry problem: the dated regulatory trigger (2026-10-28) sits BEFORE the payoff, and the first quarter that actually reads it is Q4-26, reported ~March 2027. We would be paid ~14% expected to carry an unpriced documentation-regime change for three quarters. That is why this is a 5 and not a 6. The two most-feared kill channels -- competitive bidding and rate cuts -- are REFUTED on primary sources, which is what keeps it off a 4.
